dedupe_keys.name: bts border crossing entry data us land ports of entry

description: The Bureau of Transportation Statistics' border crossing data give monthly summary statistics of inbound crossings into the United States at each land port of entry on the US-Canada and US-Mexico borders. Counts are given for trucks, trains, buses, personal vehicles, passengers and pedestrians, collected at the ports of entry by U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Each row carries the port name and code, state, border, month, measure and value, with the port's latitude and longitude. The table has 276,421 rows covering January 1996 to August 2026. Coverage is national for US land borders. The data are free and in the public domain on data.bts.gov, with CSV and JSON export and an API, updated monthly. Caveats: only inbound crossings are counted, since CBP collects no comparable outbound data, and counts are monthly totals per port, not per crossing. The series support capacity planning and network flow models of cross-border road and rail freight corridors, and studies of disruption at border crossings. It complements the Border Crossings of the World dataset and the Freight Analysis Framework.
